chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Concerning a woman who sees blood, he said: If her period is less than ten days, she waits for ten days; and if her days are ten, she does not practice istiẓhār.

key_terms.أَيَّامُهَا: her established number of days of bleeding
key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman, relevant to menstrual or irregular bleeding rulings
key_terms.الْعَشَرَةِ: the limit of ten days relevant to the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرْ: to add precautionary waiting days in this legal context
key_terms.قُرْؤُهَا: her menstrual cycle or accustomed period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istiẓhār for a woman whose bleeding days reach ten?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding a woman who sees blood and how long she should wait in relation to her menstrual pattern. It distinguishes between a woman whose menstrual habit is less than ten days and one whose days are ten, stating that the latter does not extend waiting by istiẓhār.
